claim_text: We are making positive progress in improving our safety performance and we recognise that there is still much more to do as we focus on our safety culture through leadership, robust systems, engaged behaviours and safe environments.
metric_name: Total recordable injuries; TRIFR; Total lost-time injuries
value_unit: Total recordable injuries FY25;Total recordable injuries FY24;TRIFR FY25;TRIFR FY24;Total LTI FY25;Total LTI FY24
context_text: [Table]Lag indicators FY25 FY24 FY23 Total recordable injuries 19 39 58. TRIFR 10.2 10.4 16.0. Total lost-time injuries 5 2 3.
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: Some safety indicators improved, including total recordable injuries and TRIFR, but lost-time injuries increased from 2 to 5, so the claim is only partially supported.
llm_reason: The claim asserts "positive progress in improving our safety performance." The evidence substantiates improvement in Total Recordable Injuries (decreasing from 39 in FY24 to 19 in FY25) and TRIFR (decreasing from 10.4 to 10.2). However, the evidence shows Total Lost-Time Injuries increased from 2 in FY24 to 5 in FY25. This increase in lost-time injuries contradicts the unqualified assertion of overall positive progress, indicating mixed performance. The evidence supports a material part of the claim (frequency metrics) but does not verify the complete practical meaning of overall safety performance improvement due to the deterioration in severity metrics.
